narrative.overview:
**Creative North Star: "The Line Diagram"**

A learning tree is a transit line diagram. The trunk conversation is a porcelain line; each first-level branch family is a line of its own colour; every conversation is a white-ringed station; and every branch point is an interchange ring placed at the passage the learner selected. The diagram is not decoration laid over a chat app: it is the navigation. The same family colour runs from the passage underline in a reply, through the interchange ring and the address chip that leads a title, to the Contents route strip in the sidebar and the line on the map.

The world is midnight enamel by default: a deep navy ground, a deeper field for the sidebar and the docked map, and raised enamel for anything that sits on top. Light appearance swaps to a porcelain ground with midnight ink and action and the same lines darkened to AA. It is flat and dense in the way a printed network map is dense: thick round-capped lines that turn only at 45 or 90 degrees, hairline seams, condensed caps labels, and no shadow, gradient or blur. Reading is the exception to density: replies sit at a 640px measure in a large, open reading face.

The system ships as six interchangeable themes that share every role and differ only in palette (Main Line by default, then Enamel, Tunnel, Timetable, Ferry, Terminus), each with a light and a dark variant chosen separately in Settings (Dark is the default appearance).
keyCharacteristics: One colour per first-level branch family, four lines repeating; porcelain is the trunk.
Lines 5px in the sidebar, 7px on the map, round caps, 45/90 degree turns only.
Stations and interchanges are porcelain rings; the current station is filled.
Colour belongs to lines and their chips, never to running text.
Flat enamel: tonal layers and hairline seams, no shadow, gradient or blur.
One motion: a new line draws out of its interchange, then its station lands.

rules.name: The Colour Belongs to Lines Rule
rules.body: Family colour appears only as a line, a ring, a filled address chip, a passage underline, a line tick, or a line swatch in a key or legend (a short round-capped length of the line itself). Running text is never tinted to decorate; titles and current items are porcelain, everything else is ink or muted ink.

rules.name: The No Bar Beside Text Rule
rules.body: No coloured vertical or horizontal bar sits beside text as an accent. The family shows as the filled address chip that leads a title. The Contents route strip and the swatches in keys and legends are the diagram itself, not accents, and are the only places a line runs alongside text.

rules.name: The Scarlet Means Failure Rule
rules.body: Scarlet appears only when something failed, and always with words ("Reply failed") and a way forward (Retry, Cancel, a reason). It is never a brand colour, a highlight or a destructive-button decoration.

rules.name: The One Action Colour Rule
rules.body: Porcelain is the only action fill (New chat, Send, a dialog's primary); everything else is a quiet ghost control.

rules.name: The Signage Above, Reading Below Rule
rules.body: Semi Condensed is for things you navigate by: titles, caps labels, chips, the wordmark. Anything the tutor wrote is set in the reading face. The interface between the two is Barlow.

rules.name: The Caps Are Labels Rule
rules.body: Uppercase is used only for the 12px label role and the wordmark. It never sits directly above a title as a kicker; where a screen needs to say where a conversation came from, the origin line under the title carries it.

rules.name: The Fixed Columns Rule
rules.body: Columns do not reflow when state changes. State restyles the row (current, hover, failed); it never moves the layout.

rules.name: The Flat Enamel Rule
rules.body: No shadow, gradient or blur. An overlay is lifted by sitting on raised enamel with a 1.5px strong seam, not by casting a shadow. The one permitted hard colour split is the half-filled familiarity ring on Knowledge, which is a fill state, not a gradient.

rules.name: The Porcelain Seam Rule
rules.body: Menus, popovers, the passage box, dialogs and enlarged media share one frame: raised enamel, 8px corners, a 1.5px strong-seam border.

rules.name: The Routing Rule
rules.body: A line leaves its ring horizontally, turns 45 degrees, runs vertically through the centre of the gutter (at least 40px clear of any card edge) when the rise exceeds the run, turns 45 degrees again, and enters the target ring horizontally. Rings at the same height join with one straight horizontal. A child placed left of or above its parent is not drawn.

rules.name: The One Motion Rule
rules.body: Creating a branch draws the new line out of its interchange along its path in 350ms on an exponential ease-out (`cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)`), then the station ring lands (a 125ms fade). With reduced motion it appears at once. Everything else changes state without travel: hover and reveal are opacity or colour changes of 120 to 165ms.

dos: **Do** give every first-level branch family one line colour, cycling line 1 to 4, and carry it from passage underline to interchange ring, address chip, route strip and map line.
**Do** lead every conversation title with its filled address chip (4px corners).
**Do** draw lines thick and round-capped (5px sidebar, 7px map) and turn them only at 45 or 90 degrees, following the Routing Rule.
**Do** mark stations and interchanges with porcelain rings, and the current one by filling it.
**Do** set replies in Atkinson Hyperlegible Next 17px/1.68 at a 640px measure, and titles in Barlow Semi Condensed 700 (38px conversation title).
**Do** put every overlay on raised enamel with a 1.5px strong seam and 8px corners.
**Do** use one focus ring everywhere: 2px porcelain, 2px off the control. Fields show focus on their own frame instead.
**Do** pair scarlet with words and a way forward (Retry, Cancel, a reason).
**Do** take every value from the theme roles so all six themes, light and dark, stay in step.
donts: **Don't** tint running text with a family colour to decorate it.
**Don't** place a coloured bar beside text; the route strip and key swatches are the diagram, not accents.
**Don't** use scarlet for anything but a failure.
**Don't** add shadows, gradients or blur; depth is tonal enamel and seams.
**Don't** add a second motion: no sliding panels, bouncing or travel beyond the line draw.
**Don't** put a caps kicker above a title; the origin line under it says where it came from.
**Don't** add a top bar; navigation lives in the sidebar (or the narrow header and drawer).
**Don't** use a pill radius on chips or controls; full rounding is for lines, ticks and dots.
